welcome_text: Navoi region is not only a major industrial and cultural center of Uzbekistan, but also a unique area where millennia-old history meets advanced technologies. Located in the very heart of the country, on the banks of the ancient Zarafshan River, the region boasts rich natural resources, a strong industrial foundation, and a strategic orientation towards innovative development, making it a territory with huge economic potential.

paragraph_1: The Zarafshan Valley is a major industrial and cultural center of Uzbekistan, playing an important role in the country's economic development. The valley's subsoil contains deposits of gold, tungsten, phosphorites, quartz sand, cement raw materials, and limestone. Of particular importance are the gold deposits, which have created the foundation for the mining and processing industries. In addition, the most developed uranium deposits in Uzbekistan are located in this region. The area also stands out for the presence of several oil and gas fields.
paragraph_2: The leading industries of the Zarafshan region include mining, metallurgy, chemistry, energy, oil and gas, automobile manufacturing, mechanical engineering, textiles, food, as well as construction materials production. Agriculture is also well developed in cotton growing, fur farming, vegetable cultivation, melon growing, viticulture, karakul sheep breeding, and sericulture. Livestock farming is diversified. The study of world experience shows that in almost all developed countries, scientific and technical potential plays an important, and often leading, role in programs of structural economic adjustment. At the same time, special attention is paid to the regional aspects of scientific and technical policy, which has led to significant positive results in the socio-economic development of previously backward or depressed regions. In the USA, Japan, China, Canada, Germany, France, Russia and other countries, scientific and technical potential is actively used to transform the economy, improve the structure of regional economies oriented toward highly efficient technological sectors, and to solve social and environmental problems.
paragraph_3: Changes in the qualitative indicators of the economy are based on transformations in the development of production. Almost all developed countries are shifting from knowledge- and information-based economic growth to production using the latest scientific and technological achievements and information technologies. These trends are closely related to changes in the forms and methods of organizing and managing economic entities. The intellectual products of scientists, regardless of the forms of their economic activity and ownership, are in high demand in almost all industrial enterprises. The market for high-tech products is rapidly developing due to new innovative solutions in the form of ideas, technologies, and projects, and this has become one of the main factors of intensive long-term development of the republic's economic sector. At the same time, the implementation of research results is extremely important to meet the real needs of industry.
paragraph_3_cont: The conference will be attended by about 100 leading foreign scientists from different countries, more than 200 local researchers, representatives of the Uzbek mass media, ministries and agencies, senior research fellows, university students, and employees of scientific research institutes of Uzbekistan. Scientists from Uzbek universities and the Academy of Sciences, as well as leading scholars from Germany, Korea, Japan, China, England, France, USA, Italy, Australia and other countries have been invited to the conference. The conference will consist of plenary and parallel sessions, including main sessions with practical trainings. The event will also include forums and panel discussions with educational programs and seminars. Computer technologies and displays will be used to organize interactive poster-based discussions and communication platforms. We invite researchers working in various fields to discuss the latest theoretical and experimental developments.

topic_6: – INDUSTRIAL ECONOMY AND HISTORY OF THE REGION'S INDUSTRIAL HERITAGE
zarafshon_text_1: The ancient Zarafshan river, when translated from Persian, means “the river where gold flows”. This name comes from the valley enriched with gold-bearing sands. Geographically, the Zarafshan valley covers the central part of Uzbekistan, bordered by the Nurata mountains to the north, the sandy Sundukli deserts, and the Karakum and Kyzylkum deserts to the west and northwest.
zarafshon_text_2: The Zarafshan valley in Uzbekistan alternately expands and narrows. In the wider parts lie the Samarkand, Bukhara, and Karakul oases, while in the narrower parts lie the Hazar and Karakul corridors. The Samarkand oasis is located in a depression bearing the same name. Its width is 70–80 km, length 220 km, and elevation 350–905 m above sea level. To the west, the valley expands into the Bukhara oasis. It is bordered by the Kyzylkum desert to the north and west, and the Karakul plateau to the southwest. The Zarafshan valley lies at a tilted point of the Turan plate, covered with Neogene and Quaternary layers. Before the Neogene, this area was a sea. Later tectonic processes formed dry land. As the Zarafshan river’s tributaries deepened, river terraces were formed. The surrounding mountains were formed in the Paleozoic era.
zarafshon_text_3:
To the north of the Zarafshan valley lie the Oqtov mountains. North of Oqtov is the Nurota-Quyitosh depression, with an average altitude of 500–600 m. The Nurota ridge reaches 1500 m, with the highest peak Hayotboshi at 2169 m.
One of the most important resources of the Zarafshan physical-geographical region is natural gas. Gas is extracted near Jarkoq, Korovulbozor, Bukhara, and Karakul oases.
zarafshon_text_4:
The Zarafshan valley lies in the subtropical zone. Sunny, cloudless days are frequent, with about 150 kcal of radiation per 1 cm² of surface annually. Sunshine duration reaches 3000 hours per year, resulting in hot and dry summers and relatively mild winters.
The northeastern part, surrounded by mountains, is less influenced by cold air masses from the north and northeast, while in the west, their free penetration makes it relatively cooler. Thus, in the east (Samarkand), the average January temperature is -0.5°C, while in the west (Shofirkon) it is +1.5°C. In contrast, the western part is hotter in summer, with Shofirkon’s average July temperature +29.1°C, while Samarkand’s is +26°C. The surrounding mountains have colder winters and cooler summers.
Precipitation is unevenly distributed: 114–177 mm in the west, 300–350 mm in the east, and up to 881 mm in nearby mountains (Omonqotan). Evaporation exceeds rainfall several times, leading to dry, saline soils and plant desiccation. In spring, 43–50% of the annual precipitation falls, sometimes causing floods. Autumn is also mild. The first frosts occur on October 22–25 in the west, October 28 in the east, and September 30 in the mountains.
Winters are short, mild, and moderate, with snowfall making up 35–40% of annual precipitation. Snow thickness varies: in the west it lasts about 7 days (6–7 cm), in the east 15–20 days (8–13 cm), and in the mountains almost a month (25–30 cm). The main water source is the Zarafshan river, originating from glaciers in Tajikistan. Only its middle and lower streams flow through Uzbekistan, where it seeps into the sands before reaching the Amu Darya.
zarafshon_text_5:
The name “Kyzylkum” comes from Turkic, meaning “red sands”. The reddish color comes from the erosion of sediments and winds. In the northern part near the Syrdarya, like the central Karakum, ancient alluvial plains formed by deposits have a yellowish-gray color. The desert surface slopes northwestward toward the Aral Sea coast.
Kyzylkum is one of the largest deserts of Eurasia, stretching from the Aral Sea in the north to the Zarafshan river in the south, covering about 300,000 km². It borders Uzbekistan’s Navoiy region, the Syrdarya, and Amu Darya rivers.
Kyzylkum is diverse: it has huge dunes covered with saxaul and camelthorn, clay plains, uneven ridges, and even smooth surfaces resembling parquet. Rocky low mountains, mineral springs, saxaul groves, and billion-year-old ancient rocks are found here, along with present and ancient lakes. Kyzylkum is the hottest and driest place in Uzbekistan, with annual precipitation below 70 mm. Summers are extremely hot due to intense solar radiation. Its name “Red Sands” is truly justified.
alisher_navoiy_text_1: The great Uzbek poet, thinker and statesman Nizomiddin Mir Alisher Navoi was born on February 9, 1441, in Herat — the capital of the Timurid dynasty’s Khorasan province — and spent most of his life there. Navoi’s father, Giyosiddin Bahodir, was close to the Timurid court. His passion and talent for poetry awakened early.
alisher_navoiy_text_2: Admirers of Navoi’s creativity collected his poems and compiled the “First Divan” (1464–65). Later, he himself prepared the collections “Badoyi ul-bidoya” (The Beginnings of Beauty) and “Navodir un-nihoya” (Rarities of Eternity) in the 1470s. The pinnacle of Alisher Navoi’s literary career is his “Khamsa” (1483–85). He was one of the first to create a complete “Khamsa” in the Turkic language, proving that such a grand epic could be written in Turkic. The “Khamsa” consists of the epics “Hayrat ul-Abror”, “Farhod and Shirin”, “Layli and Majnun”, “Sab’ai Sayyor”, and “Saddi Iskandariy”.
alisher_navoiy_text_3: Thanks to Navoi’s genius, Turkic peoples living in different parts of the world were united, and their cultural heritage took a firm place in the treasury of world civilization. In independent Uzbekistan, understanding and honoring Navoi has been raised to the level of state policy. One of the country’s largest regions and its capital, the State Prize of Uzbekistan, the Opera and Ballet Academic Theatre, the National Library, and hundreds of cultural and educational institutions are named after the great poet.
samarkand_title_1: Samarkand: The Most Beautiful Place in Central Asia
samarkand_text_1: Samarkand is not only a beautiful city but also historically significant. After Tashkent, it is the second largest city in Uzbekistan. Like Tashkent, Samarkand was once the capital of Uzbekistan.
samarkand_text_2: Samarkand, with its magnificent architecture, spirit of harmony, tranquility, and of course its many historical mysteries and secrets, attracts tourists and scholars from all over the world.
samarkand_title_2: History of Samarkand: The Rise of a Great City
samarkand_text_3:
It is known that cities like Memphis, Rome, Babylon, and Athens were among the first centers of human civilization. However, not everyone knows that Samarkand is just as ancient as those cities. For this reason, Samarkand is called the “Rome of the East.” The city has had many names: it was called Maroqand (in the middle of the 1st millennium BC), and later Afrosiyob. It was first mentioned in the works of those who witnessed the invasion of Alexander the Great in 329 BC. However, scholars and historians confirm that Samarkand was established long before the Macedonian conquest and its history goes much further back.
Samarkand witnessed bloody wars and invasions, but over the centuries it grew stronger and more beautiful. The city absorbed the culture and influence of the Saka and Massagetae, Greeks, Mongols, and Arabs.
Undoubtedly, Samarkand reached its peak as the capital of the Timurid Empire, the largest state stretching to the Bosporus. Amir Temur created the most powerful state in the political arena. During his rule, the world’s best architects and scholars worked in Samarkand to turn the city into a jewel of the Muslim East. After Temur’s death, the empire’s power waned; it was divided among Timurid princes. Ulugbek, Temur’s grandson and the most famous heir, was a man of peace and science. He ruled Samarkand and its surroundings for forty years. Under his reign, science reached a high level. Samarkand is an open-air museum, divided into old and modern parts. Of course, if you visit Samarkand, you must first explore the old city. This place is full of mysteries, with every corner telling a story. The heart of Samarkand is Registan. The name of this world-famous square means “sandy place.” The Registan ensemble consists of three beautiful madrasahs (the 15th-century Ulugbek Madrasah, the 17th-century Sherdor Madrasah, and the Tillya-Kori Madrasah). The harmony of the three madrasahs creates an unforgettable impression.
The next stop is the mysterious Gur-Emir (meaning “Tomb of the Emir”). It was originally built for Muhammad Sultan, a grandson of Amir Temur. Since its construction, many Timurids (members of the Timurid dynasty) have been buried here. The Gur-Emir complex consists of several parts, though not all have been preserved well. Some were later restored on the occasion of Samarkand’s 660th anniversary. The marble slabs at the top of the mausoleum and Temur’s tombstone (made only of nephrite) are in excellent condition.
Another famous place is Ulugbek’s observatory, one of Samarkand’s most remarkable landmarks. It was built by Ulugbek in 1428–1429. At that time, the observatory was invaluable and unique; it was a true achievement of astronomy. It is hard to believe that this and other Samarkand observatories were built without the use of special optical instruments. Modern Samarkand is a unique city, combining the spirit of modernity with ancient historical charm. UNESCO has included Samarkand in the World Heritage list.
Samarkand is connected by rail and air to several major cities. Its road network stretches about 8,000 km. The city has many educational centers, libraries, museums, and theaters. In the center of modern Samarkand is the “El-Merosi” theater, where you can see colorful performances and displays of national costumes. When near Registan, do not miss the history and art museum, where you can see the finest exhibitions of Uzbek cultural heritage.

buxoro_title_1: Bukhara – the Jewel of the East
buxoro_text_1: Bukhara is an ancient settlement whose history dates back to the 6th century when it became the capital of the first feudal lands of the Bukhara oasis. Shahristan, the center of the principality, arose around an ancient fortress, but as crafts and trade developed, new suburbs (rabads) appeared, connected to the new fortified walls of Shahristan.
buxoro_text_2: Remains from the 16th century have survived to this day. Bukhara has preserved the true architectural treasures of the pre-Mongol period, though very few remain. One of them is the Samanid Mausoleum, built in the 9th–10th centuries. This modest building, thanks to its artistic side and logical construction, is a true architectural monument. Its construction technique, the masterful use of brick in decoration, and the foundation make it one of the finest works of world architecture.
buxoro_text_3:
One of the later architectural monuments is the Kalyan Minaret, built in 1127. The powerful foundation of the minaret is 9 meters in diameter, narrowing slightly as it rises to a height of 46 meters. The minaret stands out not only for its grandeur and decorative brickwork but also for the art with which it was built. Remarkably, it did not need major repairs for almost 800 years.
Several unique monuments of Bukhara from the 11th–12th centuries reflect the exquisite skill of the architects and their delicate ornamentation. After the Mongol invasion, large-scale construction was not carried out in Bukhara and other cities of Central Asia. However, in later centuries, construction activity significantly increased.
In the 16th century, after the establishment of the Uzbek Shaybanid dynasty, Bukhara once again became the capital of a major Central Asian state. Civil architecture played an important role in 16th-century Bukhara. One of its important ensembles is the buildings around Lyabi-Hauz, dating back to the 17th century. The oldest of them, the Kukeldash Madrasah (1568–1569), is the largest building of its kind in Central Asia. In the 18th century, individual buildings and entire ensembles of Bukhara played a significant role in city construction, and this remains the case today.

navoiy_text_1: Today, Navoi has become one of the leading industrial centers of Uzbekistan: the Navoi Mining and Metallurgical Plant, employing thousands of people; Uzbekistan's largest company «Qizilqumsement» JSC; the world-renowned NavoiAzot association producing fertilizers and ammonia; the basis of the region’s energy sector – Navoi Thermal Power Plant; an electrochemical plant, cotton-cleaning plants, food industry enterprises – and this is not the full list of facilities of national importance.
navoiy_text_2:
Built in 1962, modernized and reconstructed in 2004-2007. The airport received international status. From January 1, 2009, Navoi Airport was transferred under the management of Korean Air for five years, with the right to extend the contract for another five years. Located at the crossroads of air routes from Asia to Europe, Navoi Airport serves as a hub for cargo from Southeast and Central Asian countries to Europe, as well as for cargo transported from Europe to Asia. Today, the airport operates 24 hours a day and is connected via cargo flights with eight cities in seven countries worldwide.
Navoi Free Industrial-Economic Zone
Located near Navoi International Airport, it serves as a base for setting up manufacturing businesses to produce various equipment and goods. Today, the zone hosts more than 15 factories.
navoiy_text_3:
In Navoi city there is a city library with 250,000 volumes, clubs, cafes and auditoriums, as well as the cultural palaces “Farhod”, “Shirin”, “Navro’z”, and the Youth Theater named after Alisher Navoi. The southern park of the city, covering 16 hectares, is considered the favorite recreation place of residents. In its alley you will find a stadium, an open pool complex with three swimming pools, summer and winter cinemas.
As the city expanded, the northern park was created as the main recreation area: it covers 70 hectares and in its center a man-made “sea” with an area of more than 20 hectares was created.
nurota_title_1: Nurota: a small town with a sacred spring
nurota_text_1:
The small town of Nurota is located at the foot of the Nurata Mountains, stretching for hundreds of kilometers to Jizzakh, Navoi, and the Kyzylkum Desert. It is the administrative and cultural center of the mountainous area of Navoi region, located almost 200 km from Samarkand.
Firstly, about the name of the town… People believe that the city was founded in the 4th century BC by the order of Alexander the Great, and in the Middle Ages it was known as "Nur" or "Nuri Bukhara". Medieval historians such as Narshakhi, Juvayni, and Istakhri referred to the ancient city as "Nur." The term "Nur" is believed to be connected with the spring in the central part of the city, because in spring and winter months, steam rises from the spring, and when the morning sun rays hit it, a rainbow appears, creating the impression that light rises from the ground.
According to legends, thousands of years ago, a fiery stone (possibly a meteorite) fell from the sky, and a healing spring appeared at the place where it landed. The name of the place is also linked to this legend. The spring complex is one of the most important Islamic centers in the region. Every year, thousands of people from neighboring cities and other countries visit this site. The complex includes an ancient fortress, a sacred spring, a Friday mosque, a dome, a bathhouse, and a hill. It is said that sometimes in spring, a strange light appears, confirming the locals' saying, “Allah gave us Nur (light)!”
Scientific information about the spring: the water temperature is always 19.5°C. The water contains 15 microelements, including gold, silver, bromine, and iodine, which give it unique healing properties. In addition, the spring is home to unique fish. This fish (marinka) is considered sacred like the spring and is not eaten by people.
nurota_text_2:
One of the unique features of Nurota is the underground water channels flowing from the sacred spring. These underground channels are called “karez” and were famous in ancient times. Today, several systems of karez still remain in Nurota and are even used today.
Nurota is located far from large industrial and tourist centers, with a population of 25,000 people, where everyone knows each other. The hospitality of the locals leaves a deep impression on tourists and pilgrims who visit this beautiful town every year.
sarmish_title_1: Sarmishsoy Gorge – Land of Ancient Petroglyphs
sarmish_text_1:
Our homeland is rich in sacred sites and monuments. In Navbahor district of Navoi region lies an open-air museum — the Sarmishsoy gorge, famous for its ancient rock carvings.
Sarmishsoy is the valley in Uzbekistan that has preserved the largest number of unique petroglyphs. According to research, 5–7 thousand years ago, the domestication of animals took place here, reflected in the rock art.
The gorge and its surroundings contain more than 10,000 petroglyphs. Most of the carvings are concentrated along 22.5 km of rocky surfaces.
Archaeological finds from the late 2nd millennium BC include bones of wild bulls, mountain goats, argali, and yaks. By the early 1st millennium BC, these animals had completely disappeared.
Known as the “open-air museum,” the site has been studied by scientists since 1966.
Today, Sarmishsoy is recognized not only nationally but also internationally as a cultural monument left by our ancestors.
sarmish_text_2:
Sarmishsoy is considered one of the earliest human settlements, with petroglyphs dating back to the 4th–1st millennia BC.
The “Sarmish” nature park covers 5,000 hectares.
In 2009, Sarmishsoy was declared a natural archaeological museum-reserve.
Sarmishsoy is included in the UNESCO World Heritage list.
The area is home to 650 species of plants from 62 families.
The complex has been studied by scientists since 1966.
Researchers believe people lived here as early as the Paleolithic era (300,000–15,000 years ago).
conference: MINING AND METALLURGY INDUSTRY IN NAVOI REGION
conference_p1:
When we talk about the Kyzylkum region of Navoi province, we imagine a generous land whose depths contain countless natural resources – gold and silver, marble and phosphorite, uranium and quartz, turquoise and limestone, almost all chemical elements of the periodic table. 
Mining, metallurgy, chemical, and energy industries are developing in the region. 
Today, more than 2,700 deposits and promising ore sites of various minerals have been identified, including about 100 types of mineral raw materials, more than 60 of which are already involved in production. More than 900 deposits have been discovered, with proven reserves estimated at 970 billion USD. It should be noted that the total mineral resource potential is 3.3 trillion USD. Every year, minerals worth about 5.5 billion USD are extracted, while reserves worth another 6.0–7.0 billion USD are added. From this perspective, studying the development issues of the Kyzylkum region, which is a unique economic and geographical complex with huge mineral reserves, is of great interest. The socio-economic development of the region is primarily connected with the largest enterprise – Navoi Mining and Metallurgical Combinat (NMMC). 
The Navoi Mining and Metallurgical Combinat, a state enterprise, is not only known in Uzbekistan as a multi-industry company but also famous worldwide. Various products are manufactured for export and for different sectors of the economy. In terms of proven and forecast reserves of gold, uranium, copper, tungsten, potassium salts, phosphorites, kaolins, and others, Uzbekistan is among the world’s top ten countries. 
Despite the wide range of products produced by NMMC, mining remains the key priority of industrial development. Gold and uranium are the main products. The enterprise carries out a full production cycle – from exploration, ore extraction, and processing, to obtaining refined gold (999.9) and uranium oxide. This shows that NMMC was established as a mining and metallurgical enterprise aimed at a complete production process.
conference_p2:
NMMC is the only operator in Uzbekistan that produces uranium and exports it as finished uranium oxide. The mineral resource base of uranium mining consists of 20 deposits and 10 promising areas. The uranium industry is steadily developing by increasing production at existing enterprises and commissioning new facilities. 
At the time of Uzbekistan’s independence, processing of gold ores and production of refined gold was carried out only at one hydrometallurgical plant – HMZ-2. Today, the gold production complex of NMMC includes four hydrometallurgical plants, one dump leaching mine, and one gold processing plant. Compared to 1991, ore processing at NMMC has tripled, and gold production has increased by more than 40%.
conference_p3:
The plant has developed and implemented unique innovative technologies. At HMZ-3, an improved flotation technology for sulfide ores was introduced. A bacterial oxidation method for high-sulfur concentrates, adapted to the Kyzylkum conditions, was launched. Sorption cyanidation technology of bacterial oxidation products was also implemented. 
NMMC has a unique software and technical complex that makes it possible to build mathematical models of underground resources and solve problems of industrial reserves evaluation, optimal mining schedules, and the final and intermediate shapes of open pits. This extends the stable operation of hydrometallurgical plants for the next 100 years and optimizes the mining and processing complexes. 
According to the 2017–2026 development program, serious tasks have been set for the plant. In recent years, investment projects have been successfully implemented, such as the construction of the 5th hydrometallurgical plant based on the Auminzo-Amantoy gold ore deposit, the construction of a waste processing complex – the “Gold Smelting and Extraction Shop,” the development of the 5th stage of Muruntau open-pit reserves, and landscaping projects. Technologies for extracting gold from refractory ores at the Kokpatas and Daugiztau deposits of the Northern Mining Administration’s 3rd hydrometallurgical plant have been implemented. 
The plant has commissioned dozens of production and social facilities, such as the “Gujumsoy” mine of the Zarmitan industrial site of the Southern Mining Administration, a cattle farm for 300 heads in the Chorloq area of Koshrabot district (Samarkand region). After full reconstruction, the “Kozmunchoq” kindergarten in Nurabad was put into operation. Soon, a unit related to rhenium extraction from technological solutions of the 4th geotechnological mine of the 5th Mining Administration will be launched. A livestock complex for 4,000 sheep in Tomdi district and the “Konchi” health center in Uchkuduk were put into operation after major repairs. 
The high qualifications of the plant’s specialists make it possible to solve problems related to the development of underground resources and the technological issues of ore mining, transportation, and processing.
conference_p4: Close cooperation has been established with large industrial research and scientific institutes. Inter-sectoral cooperation is rapidly developing. In short, large-scale reforms and innovations carried out in the interests of the people increase the well-being of citizens and strengthen confidence in the future. The innovative foundation of any state’s economic development is innovation, which ensures sustainable economic growth and the country’s participation in the global division of labor. At the current stage of socio-economic development, the rise of productive forces and continuous development of production capacity begins with a flow of scientific ideas leading to new types of engineering and technology.
chemical:
Today, the chemical industry of Uzbekistan, which has significant production, raw material and scientific-technical potential, is one of the leading sectors of the economy. It makes a great contribution to the development of the republic's economy and export potential. The chemical industry, which has strategic importance in the economy of the Republic and Central Asia, has a strong production and technical base and all the necessary conditions for long-term development in the future – large deposits of natural gas, gas condensate, sulfur, phosphorite, sylvinite, sodium chloride, limestone and others.
Uzbekistan’s chemical industry has a long history of development. The first chemical enterprises were created in the early 1930s. Taking into account the demand for mineral fertilizers and pesticides in agriculture, a number of large chemical enterprises were built in Uzbekistan, which later became the foundation for the creation of the most powerful chemical complexes in Central Asia.
The company’s existing structure makes it possible to carry out research, produce chemical products, distribute them and deliver to final consumers within a comprehensive policy. The production capacity of the company’s enterprises fully meets Uzbekistan’s domestic demand for chemical products, as well as provides for their regular export. Depending on the type of products, the company’s enterprises can be divided into four main production complexes:
– production of mineral fertilizers and inorganic substances;
– production of organic chemistry, synthetic fibers and polymer materials;
– production of chemical reagents for energy, gold mining and chemical industries;
– production of chemical plant protection products.
Products such as nitrogen and phosphate fertilizers, acetic acid, sodium chlorate, sodium cyanide, nitric acid and others meet the needs of the domestic market and partly the markets of neighboring countries in Central Asia. In terms of production volume and variety of nitrogen and phosphate fertilizers, “Uzkimyosanoat” is the largest producer of ammonia, urea, ammonium nitrate, ammonium sulfate, ammophos, superphosphate and nitrophos in Central Asia, holding a leading position in the region.
In the Zarafshan region, there are several large chemical enterprises:
– “Navoiyazot” JSC produces caustic soda, chlorine and chlorine products, chemical reagents for the gold mining industry, polyacrylamide, methanol, polyacrylon and ethylene fiber. According to the project of a French company, in 2002 the production of chlorine-magnesium defoliant and sodium chlorate was launched, ensuring high-quality production.
– At “Samarkandkimyo” JSC, specialists of “Uzkimyosanoat” together with scientists of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan developed and implemented a technology for processing Jeroy phosphorites, resulting in a new type of fertilizer – nitro-calcium phosphate (an analogue of nitrophos). This technology is based on the decomposition of phosphorites with nitric acid and is more environmentally friendly compared to existing methods.
– “Elektrokimyo Plant” JSC JV produces high-quality effective pesticides for agriculture. Currently, the company is actively pursuing an investment policy. Organizational measures are being taken to modernize and reconstruct large ammonia production capacities using the latest developments of local and foreign engineering companies, aiming to save energy and ensure high efficiency.
The chemical industry of Uzbekistan is a rapidly developing sector. By the end of 2006, industrial production grew by 114.8% compared to 2005, and exports grew by 129.0%. In recent years, enterprises of “Uzkimyosanoat” have done a lot of work to enter large markets in Asia, such as China, Iran, Turkey, Afghanistan, as well as Eastern Europe and the Baltic countries.
To further develop enterprises included in “Uzkimyosanoat”, a program for the development of the chemical industry until 2010 was adopted, which included:
– modernization and technological re-equipment of fertilizer production;
– optimization of the range of chemical products in accordance with market demand;
– gradual decommissioning of obsolete facilities and construction of modern ones;
– establishment of production of new knowledge-intensive chemical products for domestic and foreign markets.
As part of the development program, an investment program was developed that includes a number of promising projects. Their implementation will ensure a new stage in the development of chemistry in Uzbekistan.
A program for the development of the chemical industry until 2021 was also developed to carry out structural reforms, modernize and diversify the chemical industry, ensure deep processing of rich mineral resources, expand the volume and range of export-oriented finished chemical products, and attract foreign investment. The implementation of measures for modernization, technical re-equipment, introduction of innovative technologies and creation of new industries based on modern energy- and resource-saving technologies will give a strong impetus to Uzbekistan’s entry into new markets and increase its competitiveness in the global market.
As a result of the program, the production of more than 20 new types of products will be launched, including polyvinyl chloride, tires, conveyor belts, agricultural tires, carbon, potassium sulfate, potassium hydroxide and others. This will ensure diversification of manufactured products. In particular, by 2021 the share of non-food products will increase from 24% to 44%, and from 2022 – to more than 50%.
The future of chemical technology lies in the production of environmentally friendly mineral fertilizers, in other words, following a path that minimizes impact on the ecological balance of nature. This, in turn, stimulates the expansion of safe food reserves for humanity.
As one of the leading sectors of our country, the chemical industry makes a significant contribution to the development of the economy and its export potential, fully satisfies domestic demand for chemical products, and steadily increases their supply to foreign markets.

Uzbekistan’s energy system is the largest in Central Asia. The total installed capacity of power plants is about 14,140.6 MW. Nearly 85 percent of electricity generation comes mainly from natural gas, with the remainder from hydropower. In 2019, Uzbekistan increased electricity production by 1.4 percent compared to the same period in 2018.
The growth of gross domestic product (8–8.5% annually) is accompanied by an increase in energy consumption.
At the current stage of economic development, the main goal of the electric power industry is to meet the growing demand for electricity, modernize and reconstruct existing power plants and grids, build new generation capacities based on highly efficient technologies, improve electricity metering systems, develop fuel and energy resources, and utilize renewable energy sources.
The development of the power sector until 2021 provides for the implementation of 62 investment projects covering all areas of energy, which will ensure: further improvement of generation technologies, increased efficiency of natural gas use, implementation of measures to reduce the energy intensity of industrial products; maintaining the trend of rapid development of the country’s hydropower resources; further diversification of the fuel and energy balance through the use of non-traditional renewable energy sources (construction of wind and solar power plants); formation of an optimal configuration of main electric grids to increase system stability while meeting the growing needs of the economy, population, and exports; strengthening the stability of the unified energy system, improving the reliability of power supply to consumers, and enhancing the country’s energy security.
To date, in the Zarafshan Valley, losses of electricity on high-voltage lines are being eliminated or reduced, losses in transformers and electrical installations are decreasing, optimal operating modes are being determined, and research is being carried out on the development of energy-saving devices.
Nuclear energy. The construction of nuclear power plants is of great importance. Such plants will produce the cheapest electricity with long-term guarantees. According to experts, by 2030 the demand for electricity in Uzbekistan will double to 117 billion kWh. Without introducing new energy sources, the current deficit would reach 48 billion kWh. The country’s annual electricity demand is 69 billion kWh. Construction of the first two power units by the state corporation Rosatom will add 2,400 MW (21 billion kWh per year) to the national energy balance. According to various estimates, in 2030 the plant will produce between 14 and 18 percent of the country’s electricity.
Solar energy. Uzbekistan has enormous renewable energy potential, with solar energy being the most promising. The country’s climate and geography make it possible to actively use solar energy for industrial-scale electricity and heat generation. Solar power is a renewable, convenient, easy-to-use, and promising source of energy. Uzbekistan’s gross solar potential is estimated at nearly 51 billion tons of oil equivalent, and its technical potential at 177 million tons of oil equivalent—more than three times the current fossil fuel production.
Uzbekistan’s strong solar radiation and advanced photovoltaic technologies enable the government to expand the use of renewables. By 2031, it plans to meet more than 20% of total energy needs from renewable sources, including solar.
The Kyzylkum region is one of the sunniest areas in the country. During summer, solar energy can be used for 15–16 hours a day. Given the remoteness of some settlements and shepherd households from centralized grids, providing them with solar power is considered cost-effective. The region experiences more than 3,000 hours of sunshine annually, with 1,200–2,000 kWh of energy falling on each square meter.
In the Kyzylkum area, each square meter receives 1,600–2,000 kWh per year, which creates significant opportunities for generating electricity and heat. Under the state program, a 100 MW photovoltaic plant is planned in Karmana district, and a 1 MW plant in Zarafshan city.
Wind energy. Uzbekistan has suitable wind resources for successful development of wind power. Based on the Atlas developed by the company, Uzbekenergo identified two promising sites — one in the region and one in southern Karakalpakstan. On each site, meteorological masts 85 meters high were installed with instruments to measure wind speed and direction, as well as air density and temperature. Data is transmitted online via satellite for analysis. This analysis helps calculate electricity generation and determine the optimal capacity of wind turbines.
Biomass use. In Uzbekistan, the use of biomass in agriculture, households, and family farms has long been practiced. Manure is used in aerobic composting, anaerobic digestion (biological decomposition), and directly as organic fertilizer. Biomass has also been a traditional energy source for biogas production. Uzbekistan’s biomass potential is estimated at about 3,500 MWh.
Geothermal resources are found in almost all regions of the country. Research has identified eight hydrothermal resources. The gross potential of geothermal waters is estimated at 244,200 tons of oil equivalent, though the technical potential has not yet been determined. The average temperature of geothermal waters is 45.5 ºC, with the highest recorded in Bukhara (56 ºC) and Syrdarya (50 ºC) regions. In the future, this heat could be used almost everywhere, since at depths of 4,000–6,000 meters, rock temperatures range from 70 to 300 ºC. Despite good research on geothermal reservoirs, the use of thermal waters is still in its early stages. Development of thermal springs is included in the national energy program.
Opportunities. The Navoi Free Industrial-Economic Zone attracts foreign investors and enables the production of components for solar and wind power plants.
Projects for the use of solar and biogas energy are supported by funding from the Asian Development Bank and other international financial institutions.
According to experts, Uzbekistan’s geographic location and climate provide excellent opportunities for such projects. With more than 320 sunny days per year, the country surpasses many regions of the world.
According to estimates by the Asian and World Banks, Uzbekistan’s total solar potential exceeds 51 billion tons of oil equivalent. This means, experts note, that electricity production could be 40 times higher than current consumption.
It should be noted that dozens of solar energy processing plants are operating in different regions, providing stable electricity and heat to individual facilities. Production of silicon photovoltaic batteries has been launched, taking into account local natural conditions. Compact, low-power solar devices for charging mobile phones, laptops, and tablets are also being developed and have successfully passed field tests.
The most active and effective scientific research is being conducted in the use of solar energy for hot water and heating, electricity generation via photovoltaic and thermodynamic conversions, and the creation of low-potential stations for thermal processing of materials and structures.
ecology: The natural conditions of the Zarafshan valley are favorable for the development of agriculture. The Zarafshan River, numerous mountain streams, as well as underground waters make it possible to irrigate large tracts of land. Along with rich gas fields in the lower reaches of the Zarafshan River, the valley and adjacent areas are rich in energy resources important for the entire economy. The vast pastures of the surrounding desert and mountainous areas contribute to the development of karakul sheep breeding and livestock farming. Here, 65% of all pastures of the republic are concentrated; nowhere else in Uzbekistan are such conditions for grazing sheep. Therefore, the district stands out with high economic performance. It is the largest producer of karakul in the republic, with 2/3 of karakul sheep grazed on local pastures. Karakul sheep, being a domestic breed, produce four types of valuable products under desert pasture conditions: karakul pelts, wool, meat, and milk. The main product, karakul pelts, is in high demand both domestically and internationally and is an important export commodity. No other sheep breed can use the rare desert plants as efficiently as the karakul. Due to its endurance, this breed covers long distances and feeds on scarce desert vegetation. The region’s soil, flora, and fauna are highly diverse. Over 3000 plant species grow in Uzbekistan, 9% of them endemic. Uzbekistan’s flora and fauna share similarities with the Caucasus and the Middle East, especially Iran. The republic is home to more than 90 species of mammals, about 60 reptiles, 400 bird species, and over 40 fish species. In spring, ephemeral plants grow rapidly (annual plants that sprout, bloom, set seed, and wither within a short spring). In summer, grasses and flowers turn yellow and dry up. Desert plants are adapted to hot and dry climates: they have long roots, tiny or no leaves, which minimizes moisture evaporation. In sandy deserts grow wormwood, yulgun, sand acacia, reeds, licorice, and saxaul. Saxaul holds sand in place; its wood is dense and sinks in water. In saline soils grow wormwood, saltwort, and other desert plants. The desert plains of the Zarafshan valley are used as pastures for karakul sheep and camels. Many useful plants grow here, used in medicine and chemical industry. Samarkand region is one of the oldest viticulture areas. Grapes were cultivated here three thousand years ago. In 1984 Samarkand region ranked first in Uzbekistan in vineyard area and harvest. More than 100 grape varieties are grown: white kishmish, black kishmish, nimrang, pink toyfi, kattaqorgoni, husayni, sultani, etc. Samarkand is also a major center for raisin production. Ecology of the Zarafshan Valley Uzbekistan’s underground resources are rich in oil, gas, coal, sulfur, salt, phosphorites, construction materials, etc. In the Nurata mountains and near Khujand, marble of different colors is quarried – white, pink, reddish, gray. It is used in electrical engineering, construction, and the restoration of historical monuments (Samarkand, Khiva, Bukhara). Gazgan marble has been used to decorate metro stations. The Zarafshan valley lies on the inclined part of the Turan Plate, covered with Neogene and Quaternary sediments. Before the Neogene, this was a sea. Later tectonic processes formed land. Deepening of the Zarafshan river created terraces. The Oktov mountains lie to the north, with the highest point being Hayotboshi peak (2169 m). Natural gas is extracted in Jarko‘q, Karavulbazar, Bukhara, and Karakul areas. The valley is located in the subtropics, with many sunny days – up to 3000 hours of sunshine per year. In Samarkand, January averages -0.5°C, Shofirkon +1.5°C; in July Samarkand +26°C, Shofirkon +29.1°C. The main river is Zarafshan, which near Samarkand splits into Akdarya (north) and Karadarya (south), rejoining at Khatirchi. Between them lies Miyonkol island (100 km long, 15 km wide). Average annual flow is 165 m³/s, minimum 30–35, maximum 930 m³/s. Water is widely used for irrigation; the Kattakurgan reservoir has been built. The area has significant underground water reserves. Paleogene and Neogene aquifers contain fresh water suitable for drinking, while Anthropogene layers are slightly saline. Thermal mineral waters are also present. The soils are soft and prone to erosion. Improper use of pastures and irrigated lands causes wind and irrigation erosion.

By the middle of the 20th century, as a result of the search for underground resources in the vast territories of Kyzylkum, which had not been explored for centuries, uranium deposits were discovered in Uchkuduk in 1958, and the Navoi Mining and Metallurgical Combine (NMMC) was established for their extraction and processing.

The foundation, development, and transformation of the combine into a large enterprise is the result of the labor of dedicated, courageous, and strong-willed people capable of solving the most complex engineering, technical, and social problems. They spared no effort and devoted their lives to this cause. Today, this large enterprise plays an important role in strengthening the economic power of our country.

During the years of independence, thanks to the hard work of highly qualified employees and the scientifically based strategy of technical re-equipment carried out in the divisions of the combine, extraction and processing increased, product quality improved, and export volumes grew. NMMC became one of the ten largest companies in the world producing gold and uranium.

In the years of independence, broad opportunities were opened for modernization and diversification of production. This, in turn, ensured the rapid and comprehensive development of the combine. Especially in the last decade, enterprises equipped with advanced technologies and producing globally competitive products have been built. In particular, the technology of bacterial oxidation of sulfide ores was introduced at Hydrometallurgical Plant No. 3. At the Central Mining Administration, a heap leaching plant for gold extraction and an emulsion explosives plant were launched at the Muruntau deposit; at the Southern Mining Administration, Hydrometallurgical Plant No. 4 was constructed; and at the Muruntau mine, a unique high-capacity steep-incline conveyor was put into operation.

With the support of our government, the construction of new industrial enterprises, their equipping with advanced technologies, and the implementation of investment projects are constantly expanding. This ensures the growth of gold ore and uranium extraction and processing.

As a result of technical and technological updates, the production of gold, silver, and uranium in our country has almost doubled. The gold bars of the combine with a fineness of "999.9" have become a brand of Uzbekistan on the world precious metals exchanges.

The creation of modern industries in Uzbekistan and their gradual development serve to increase the economic potential of the country. In 2017, at the initiative of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, the foundation stone for the construction of Hydrometallurgical Plant No. 5 was laid, and work is being carried out at a rapid pace. Today, the Zarafshan Valley has turned into a major construction site. These grand plans and construction works enrich today’s rapid reforms. The combine team is mobilizing all its strength to fulfill these tasks.

The path of innovative development. In a market economy, every company must have a clear innovation strategy. Production cannot be imagined without innovative technologies. In recent years, long-term and well-thought-out strategies for innovation research have been carried out at the combine, and production capacities have been created based on resource- and energy-saving technologies. Most importantly, knowledgeable and initiative local personnel capable of managing modern enterprises with innovative technologies have been trained.

In 2018, in order to develop research and innovation activities, an Innovation Center was established at the combine, and the "NMMC Innovation Development Program - 2026" was adopted. The implementation of 105 innovative projects in this program will create a solid foundation for increasing the efficiency of gold ore and uranium extraction and processing, reducing production costs, and expanding the range of export-oriented products.

Today, more than 10,000 specialists with higher education, including 31 candidates of sciences and 7 doctors of sciences, work at the combine. For the first time in the mining and metallurgical industry of Uzbekistan, in 2017 a group of scientists and specialists from NMMC and Navoi State Mining Institute was awarded the "Best Inventor" gold medal by the World Intellectual Property Organization under the UN for developing a technology for extracting gold from complex ores. This is a high recognition of the science of our country.

The combine cooperates with many companies located in different parts of the world, from the USA and Canada to Australia and Japan.

Strong ties have been established with famous firms such as Orenstein & Koppel, Atlas Copco, Wirtgen, Caterpillar, Euclid, NM Rothschild & Sons Limited, TACIS, Marubeni, Bridgestone, Shell, Spekto Analytical Instruments, Hitachi, Nissho Iwai, LRS Planung und Technologie, Wirth, Dobersek, Allweiler, GERMTD, Grundfos, NUKEM GmbH, Siemens, and MAN TAKRAF. Business delegations regularly visit Navoi, contracts are signed, and joint projects are developed.

NMMC is one of the initiators and founders of the American-Uzbekistan Chamber of Commerce. This non-governmental organization, established in September 1993, unites companies interested in developing and improving investment and trade relations between Uzbekistan and the United States.

The combine also cooperates with international organizations dealing with environmental protection. Specialists and technical experts from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) have visited the enterprise many times, studied the environmental situation, and received full answers to all questions. NMMC participates in the EU’s "TASIS" environmental program and closely cooperates with foreign companies commissioned by the European Commission to implement this program.

In the fall of 1996, members of the IAEA delegation, including specialists in radiation protection from Sweden and uranium consumers, visited the combine and highly appreciated the environmental measures taken there.

NMMC pays special attention to the development of intellectual property; many patents and certificates have been obtained for inventions, utility models, industrial designs, and databases. Every year applications are submitted for patents, including to international patent organizations. Rationalization proposals from workers and engineers are implemented in production, products are manufactured in accordance with international standards, and modern technologies are rapidly introduced. The great attention paid to science in our country contributes to the growth of scientific and technical potential, the expansion of the integration of science and production, the modernization of the economy, and, most importantly, the improvement of people’s welfare.

Qualified personnel — the key to success. The main personnel policy of the combine is to provide current and newly built facilities with qualified specialists and workers in a timely and high-quality manner and to train skilled personnel. The personnel policy is aimed at their professional growth, the formation of reserves, advanced training, and the development of practical skills.

Special attention is paid to the training of young specialists and highly skilled workers in the six training centers of the combine. Today, about 93% of 60,000 employees and more than 90% of managers are local specialists — this is the result of systematic work carried out to train the necessary engineering personnel in this field.

Today, responsible tasks in enterprise management are entrusted to modern, creative, initiative, intellectually capable, and patriotic young personnel. They are active in all areas of the combine, distinguished by a new approach to every issue.

Social sphere: human interests in focus. In our country, great attention is paid to improving living conditions, providing comprehensive social assistance to citizens. Our people feel the results of the reforms being implemented.

Ensuring human interests and social protection is one of the main directions at the combine. All efforts are aimed at improving the living conditions of employees, ensuring their health, effective recreation, and meaningful leisure.

Employees of the combine are provided with modern housing. In recent years, more than 1,300 people have received new apartments.

Today, special attention is paid to strengthening the health of employees. The medical department and its five regional branches provide qualified medical care to employees and their families.

Special attention is paid to the formation of moral and ethical values among employees, especially young people, to the development of their intellectual potential, consciousness and worldview, and to the promotion of reading culture. Today, 11 libraries with a collection of more than 550,000 books serve employees and the public.

All conditions have been created for recreation and a healthy lifestyle for employees and their families. The "Metallurg", "Gornyak" and "Nurabad" sanatoriums, the "Zarafshan" boarding house, and the "Tudakul" recreation center are equipped with modern medical equipment. In 2019, the "NMMC" sanatorium for 150 people was commissioned in Zomin district of Jizzakh region.

In recent years, the "Neptune" swimming pool in Zarafshan has been overhauled, the "Sogdiana" stadium in Navoi has been reconstructed, the "Yangi Hayot" sports complex and an indoor swimming pool have been built in Zafarobod settlement. The "Orzu" amusement park was created in Uchkuduk and became a favorite place for residents. Taking into account the interests and needs of young people, the modern "Kelajak" youth center was opened in Uchkuduk. Children’s water parks were built in Zarafshan and Zarmitan, beautiful musical fountains were erected in Navoi, Zarafshan and Zafarobod. In 2018, the "Kozmunchoq" kindergarten in Nurobad was reconstructed and put into operation.

Special attention is paid to children — the future of the country. In the summer season, more than 10,000 employees’ children rest in 11 summer camps and city children’s camps, participate in various circles, and strengthen their knowledge and skills. The children’s health camps "Pahlavon", "Bolajon", "Sarmish", "Sogdiana", "Zarafshan" and "Kelajak" are located in picturesque natural areas. In addition, 9 cultural institutions and children’s creativity houses operate in the system, with more than 170 artistic circles and amateur groups functioning.

These people have different professions, but from the manager to the ordinary worker, everyone is united by their dedication to their work.
Today, JSC 'NavoiAzot' is a multi-profile industrial and production complex that is rapidly developing, has its place among international partners, and implements programs for the production of mineral fertilizers, chemical reagents, and other small-tonnage chemical products.
The enterprise produces over 30% of Uzbekistan's chemical products and is one of the base segments of JSC 'UzKimesanoat'. 'NavoiAzot' covers industry, transport, agriculture, fuel and energy complex, as well as almost all sectors of services, science, culture, and education.
One of the main goals of the enterprise is to meet consumer demands and high product quality standards. Therefore, we were among the first in the republic to implement an international quality management system, which ensures compliance with technological regulations, confirms product compliance with standards, and allows enterprise specialists to manage production at the level of world standards, enhancing the company's reputation both nationally and internationally.
The divisions of JSC 'NavoiAzot' carry out a full production cycle. New technologies are being mastered here, automated systems for production and management are implemented, existing complexes are modernized, and new production facilities are built.

The power of JSC 'NavoiAzot's' technology, its progressive character, the bold innovative and scientifically grounded ideas of its workers and engineers, high professional skills, and team unity make it an example for many enterprises and a pride of independent Uzbekistan.
One of the main objectives is to improve the professional training and classification of personnel, demonstrating that the enterprise's main wealth is highly qualified specialists. In a team of over 10,000 employees, special attention is paid to stability, creating social protection conditions for workers, and increasing labor efficiency.
Special attention is given to children, ensuring their comprehensive development and healthy growth — this is a guarantee of future success. The development strategy of JSC 'NavoiAzot' is based on the nationwide investment policy.
To improve product quality, reduce costs, and ensure the production of competitive products in domestic and foreign markets, investment projects aimed at modernizing technologies and providing new equipment for production are actively implemented.
Investment projects aimed at modernizing existing production and technical upgrades are actively implemented to improve product quality and reduce costs to ensure the competitiveness of the enterprise's products in Uzbekistan and on the world market.
In accordance with the decrees of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan dated November 17, 2014, No. PP-2264 'On measures to implement investment projects of 2015 in the Republic of Uzbekistan', dated December 16, 2014, No. 2272 'On measures to implement investment projects for the construction of polyvinyl chloride (PVC), caustic soda, and methanol production complexes at JSC NavoiAzot', and dated March 4, 2015, No. UP-4707 'On measures to ensure structural renewal, modernization and diversification for 2015–2019', the following projects are being implemented at JSC 'NavoiAzot':
- construction of ammonia and urea production facilities;
- construction of PVC, caustic soda, and methanol production complexes;
- organization of nitric acid production;
- modernization and reconstruction of energy supply facilities, replacing measuring instruments with modern ones, implementing automated control systems for technological processes.

The Joint Stock Company “Navoi Thermal Power Plant” is a major source of heat and electricity, supplying industrial and production enterprises of the region as well as the residential and communal sector.

Construction of the station, which is among the major thermal power plants of the national energy system, began in 1960, and the first unit with a capacity of 25 MW was connected to the grid on February 8, 1963. In 2014, the plant supplied 8,801,510 thousand kWh of electricity and 2,000,040 thousand Gcal of heat energy. From the connection of the first unit to the grid until the first December of 2015, 331.673 billion kWh of electricity and 147,843 thousand Gcal of heat energy were delivered to consumers. In January 2015, the power grid received 820,556,600 kWh of electricity, and 2,039,856 Gcal of heat energy were delivered to consumers. Initially, the station construction started as part of the Navoi Mining and Metallurgical Plant and from 1965 it was transferred to the Ministry of Energy of Uzbekistan.

The electric and heat capacities of the station include: 25 MW each, total 50 MW — units 1 and 2 (2 TGM-151 boilers and 2 VPT-25-4 turbogenerators); 150 MW each, total 300 MW — TGM-94 boiler and PVK-150-130 turbogenerator for units 3 and 4; 50 MW each — 2 R-50-130 turbogenerators, 1 PT-60-130 turbogenerator, 4 TGM-84 boilers; 160 MW each, total 320 MW — TGM-94 boiler and K-160-130 turbogenerator for units 8 and 9; total 420 MW, 210 MW each — TGMYe-206 boiler and K-210-130 turbogenerator for units 11 and 12. From the fourth quarter of 2012, a combined-cycle gas and steam plant with a capacity of 478 MW was also commissioned.

To ensure the production of goods that meet international standards and are in demand in global markets, and to establish modern high-tech industries, favorable conditions are created for attracting foreign investments, primarily direct investments. Additionally, to develop the industrial potential, production, transport-transit, and social infrastructure of the Navoi region, the first free zone in Uzbekistan – the Navoi Free Industrial-Economic Zone (FIEZ) – was established in the Karmana district of Navoi region based on the Decree of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan dated December 2, 2008, No. PF-4059 “On the establishment of a free industrial-economic zone in Navoi region.”

The total area of the Navoi FIEZ is 564 hectares. Due to its proximity to Navoi International Airport, the E-40 highway, and an international railway, it has access to the multimodal transport and logistics network of Navoi region.

The Navoi FIEZ operates under a special legal regime, which includes tax, currency, and customs regimes, simplified entry, stay, and exit procedures, as well as permits for non-resident citizens to work, and provides broad exemptions from taxes, customs, and other mandatory payments. The FIEZ’s duration is 30 years, with the possibility of extension.

Registered business entities in the Navoi FIEZ are exempt from land, property, income taxes, taxes for the development of social and communal infrastructure, single tax (for small enterprises), contributions to the Republican road fund, and reconstruction and equipment funds for educational and medical institutions, depending on the amount of direct investment: 3–10 million euros – for 7 years; 10–30 million euros – for 10 years, with the next 5 years’ profit tax and single tax at 50% of the current rate; more than 30 million euros – for 15 years, with the following 10 years’ profit tax and single tax at 50% of the current rate.

The main activities of business entities in the Navoi FIEZ are directly related to the production of high-tech, globally competitive products, implementing modern foreign production capacities, equipment, technological lines and modules, and innovative technologies.

The Navoi FIEZ has all the conditions for creating an industrial complex covering the full production cycle – from raw materials to finished products.

The concept of establishing the Navoi FIEZ and the selected priorities determine the scheme for placing enterprises by sectors and directions. Currently, 19 enterprises operate in the FIEZ. Since its establishment, a total of 122 million USD has been invested, about 35% of which are direct foreign investments. By the end of 2015, products worth 184.4 billion UZS were produced, and goods worth 5.1 million USD were exported, three times higher than the same period in 2014.

tezis:
The theses are published in English, Uzbek and Russian.

General requirements
Theses of no more than 2 pages are accepted. Use Microsoft Word on Windows for writing text, formulas, and tables. Before writing, set the following parameters: page format: A4 (210x297 mm), all margins 2.5 cm; font Times New Roman, size 12; line spacing - single; justify text; first line indent 1 cm; page orientation vertical. Images used in the article must be in jpg, gif, bmp format; images created in MS Word are not accepted. All images and tables must be numbered, labeled, centered, and italicized.

Thesis title
Title settings: use bold font; all letters capitalized; place at the top of the page; center align; do not break words; 12-pt spacing between title and author(s).

Author name and affiliation
Follow these instructions to indicate the author’s name: bold font; center aligned, first letters capitalized. Add a superscript number corresponding to the author’s affiliation. Affiliation should be in 11 pt, italic, centered, country in parentheses. Place a corresponding superscript before the affiliation. Leave 6-pt spacing between author name and affiliation.

Abstract and keywords
Leave 24 pt before the word “Abstract”, then -6 pt. The word “Abstract” should be bold, center aligned, first letter capitalized. Abstract text starts on a new line, font size 10 pt, justified. The abstract should briefly describe the article's content and present the main results and conclusions. The abstract is not part of the thesis text; it must be complete; it does not include tables, numbers, references, or mathematical expressions. Abstract should not exceed 200 words and be written in a single paragraph. Leave 6-pt spacing before keywords. Keywords should be 10 pt, justified, no more than 10 words.

Main text requirements
Leave 18-pt spacing before the main text. If the main text has sections, the main section titles (Introduction, Methodology, Results, Conclusions, and References) should be bold, first letter capitalized, left aligned. Start the text from a new line after the section title. Leave 6-pt spacing before section title.

References
Citations in the text should correspond to the reference list in square brackets, e.g.: [1, p. 277]. The reference list should match the numbering in the text. The phrase "References" should be bold, left aligned, with 18 pt before and 3 pt after.
[1] A. Einstein, “General theory of relativity,” Annalen der Physik, vol. 49, no. 7, pp. 769–822, 1916. [2] A.A. Author, "Journal/Conference Article Title," Periodical Title, vol. Volume, no. Issue, pp.-pp., Publication Year.

konferensiya_haqida_main: Conferences at NSMTU: a platform for dialogue, innovation and cooperation
konferensiya_haqida:
Conferences and forums regularly organized by NSMTU are a vital platform for effective dialogue between leading scientists, engineers of industrial enterprises, and representatives of large and medium-sized local and foreign companies. These events create a unique opportunity to comprehensively discuss the pressing issues and development prospects of the Zarafshan Valley, as well as encourage the active introduction of advanced technologies and innovative solutions into production.
Participants of the conference will not only be able to present the results of their latest research and developments, but also establish new business relations, exchange views with colleagues from various fields of science and industry, and find potential partners for joint projects. Thus, NSMTU not only effectively carries out educational and research activities, but also creates a strong and effective ecosystem for innovation and sustainable development in the Zarafshan Valley, consistently strengthening its status as one of Uzbekistan's key industrial, scientific and technological centers.

konferensiya_haqida_2: The conference will include plenary sessions with recognized leaders in their fields, as well as parallel section meetings designed for in-depth and targeted discussions on the main thematic areas.
